doc: Hull rig fragment/style library — decision 9.2 'style lives in the tool' (docs/IMPLEMENT-Phase10.md). This file pins the fragment vocabulary the authored maps were drawn with, the shared palette keys, the tier bands and the per-hull rig table, so a style fix is a data edit + rebuild, never a PNG hand-edit. Shading rule everywhere: light from NW (80-* §4.8.2) — NW-facing edges take the HI step, SE-facing the LO step; silhouette-first, readable at 1:1; authored maps are outline-less (the governor applies the 1px #101010 token outline).

palette_keys._doc: chars used by every authored string-map; hexes = the §4.8.4 hull block, amended 2026-11-04 (scripts/palette.gd hull-block constants). Block membership is per-class: hull tokens + facility tokens check against the hull block only; hull DOCS are exempt while carrying the pennant source hex (an authoring-only intermediate).

H.use: wood highlight (NW rim, castle decks; owner-invariant)

W.use: wood base (hull body, counters, boards; owner-invariant)

L.use: wood shadow (SE rim), plank seams, facility stone shadow (palace)

s.use: sail highlight (top/port edge), facility stone highlight (palace)

d.use: deep sail shade — the billow's dark flank (UW2 craft bar)

D.use: warm deck-plank tone for the oblique deck planes (UW2 craft bar)

K.use: gunports, gallery windows, rigging stays (owner-invariant like the sails)

pennants._doc: amended §4.8.4 hull block — the shared-hull pennant scheme: the authored maps draw the SOURCE hex at every masthead pennant; the governor remaps it to the owner's pennant (the only owner-variant pixel). Wood/sail/ink and the t3 HULL_GOLD trim are owner-invariant; spain is the legal identity remap. The retired owner HI/BASE/LO ramps are gone from the pipeline (their palette.gd constants remain, append-only history).

tier_bands._doc: long-axis px on the side view e/w (§4.8.7 final values, amended 2026-11-04: the profile shows the ship's length; n/s/diagonals are beam/3/4 views, canvas-fit only)

beam_fraction.note: galley-family hulls (galiot, pinnace, galley, galleass, xebec) run deliberately slim (~33-40%): oar banks and lateen rigs read narrow; judged acceptable against the silhouette-first rule at W3 authoring.

hull_body.shape: tapered elongated hull; bow_len ≈ 22% and stern_len ≈ 18% of length; transom ≈ 72% of max beam; bow tip half-width 0.6 px (pointy) unless beak
hull_body.shading: NW rim WOOD_HI, SE rim WOOD_LO, interior WOOD

keel_line.rule: center deck line from bow_len+1 to stern taper, hidden under sails

yard.rule: spar at the mast row, sail-width wide, sail hangs aft of it

square_sail.shape: rectangle sw x sh (rows aft of mast)
square_sail.shading: top+port edge SAIL_HI, bottom+starboard edge SAIL_LO

junk_battens.rule: square sail with alternating SAIL_LO rows (full-batten), top edge SAIL_HI

lateen.shape: triangle, apex at the mast, widening aft (sw x th)
lateen.shading: port half SAIL_HI, starboard half SAIL_LO

oar_row.rule: blades flank the hull (2px off the side), stations every `step` rows between the fractions

stern_castle.rule: raised deck block (fore and/or aft) with a 1px K leading edge; hw = block half-width

beak.rule: galleon bow profile rises as t^1.7 — a beaked entry within the same length

footprint_semantics.long_axis: side-view (e/w) opaque bbox x-extent on the final outlined file — all eight directions are authored maps now, so the band is measured where the ship's length actually shows (§4.8.7 amendment)
footprint_semantics.note: the ne map is the honest 45° rotation of the n ship; its bbox max under-reads the physical length by ~1/√2, so it is canvas-fit checked (≤30 px) but not banded — pinning this reading here so the governor, the manifests and group 13 measure the same thing

nao.rig: big 3-mast carrack-like: 3 square sails + forecastle + aftcastle

carrack.rig: 2 square + 1 lateen, high stern castle only

galleon.rig: 3 square sails, beaked bow, aft castle

galleass.rig: hybrid: 9 oar stations + 3 lateens, longest hull
